claim: Judge William Alsup held Anthropic's use of books to train its Claude LLMs was "exceedingly transformative" and fair use, but downloading pirated books was not.
evidence: Judge Alsup found that the use of training copies of the authors’ copyrighted works to train Anthropic’s LLMs was “exceedingly transformative” and was therefore a fair use.
excerpt:
As for the legally purchased books used to train the LLMs, Judge Alsup found this to be fair use because Anthropic simply replaced the print copies with more convenient digital ones. However, use of the pirated works was not fair use.
